title: "Silent Night, Holy Night"
subtitle: We hear the song every night we bid the day farewell. Wishing you peace, my dear.

trails.title: Wall of Gratitude
trails.description: There's a secret group in the world that does good deeds in silence—let's list all its members on this wall.

content.text:
Dear anonymous gentleman,

    The Veterans' Residence deeply appreciates your generosity. Your donations have been a great help during these difficult times. We've taken to calling you Mr. Marble, after your donation of that fine marble chair. I assume marble holds some special significance for you. If you happen to see this letter, we hope that you will one day soon come through the door and accept our thanks and hospitality. I'm sure you'll be pleased and comforted by the heart-warming sights inside the home you've so long supported, and we'd love to hear the story behind the large red button you've placed on your gifted chair.

trails.title: Paths of the Past - Anjo Nala

content.text: Those pristine wings, however, could never, ever fly across the riverbank.

items.text: "Silent Night, Holy Night"
The route from the favela to the Veterans' Residence is quite familiar to White Rum. She has ferried the doctor back and forth countless times.

items.speaker: White Rum
items.text: You ever been to a Veterans' Residence? Not many young faces there, besides Lopera. As far as the doc goes, doubtful anyone knows her real age, and even the saltiest sailor knows better than to ask a lady her age!
Sao Paulo Veterans' Residence

items.speaker: White Rum
items.text: Oh. I see that joke missed the bow, so to speak.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, no, it wasn't a bad joke at all, really.
A joke would usually warrant some kind of response.

items.speaker: White Rum
items.text: Aye, thanks for the kind words, lass, but best to leave old flotsam where it lies.
Mamãe Mariana from the Veterans' Residence brings out some snacks.
There's plenty of sugar to go round in this neck of the woods.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: Have you been filling this sweet young lady's head with your tall tales, Shippy?
The little ship used to live with the doctor in the Veterans' Residence, but today she returns alone, and neither one of her two passengers is her old roommate.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sorry to show up without proper notice.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: Don't worry about it! Any friend of Lopera is a friend of ours.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: Oh. If you'd come a couple of days earlier, we would've introduced you to Mr. Duncan and Dr. Dores.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: But they've not been around in a while.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's a shame. I was looking forward to meeting them. Hopefully we'll see them soon.
Kimberly wanders the courtyard. She's still on guard, but she seems to be oddly familiar with this place.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: You know, I knew a girl who looked just like her. A caregiver here way back in the '60s.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: Back when this place was called Heartfelt Home.
She scratches the chin of the kitten in her arms.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: But it can't be her now, can it? Besides, I'm old now, and my memory is a bit fuzzier than it used to be.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: May I see Dr. Dores's room?

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: She wouldn't mind, but please be careful not to move anything.

items.speaker: Mamãe Mariana
items.text: It's that one over there, dear. She never locks the door.
The place looks no different from the other rooms in the courtyard, but the door is slightly ajar.
Green vines hang from the roof, and the weathered walls bear the passage of time. It's a simple little home.
Kimberly stands by the door, a stray cat in her arms. She scratches its belly.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Aah!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: How dare you scratch me!
The cat leaps out of Kimberly's arms, grabs hold of one of the vines, and clambers over the wall of the Veterans' Residence.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Get back here, you fluffy rapscallion! I'll have your tail, you hear me?!
She's not as agile as she looks, or perhaps the kitten has made her soft.
She fails to catch it, instead stumbling into the door, throwing it wide open, and hitting the floor with a thud.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do be careful, Ms. Kimberly.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Ugh, how did that happen?

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: And how long have you been standing there?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Just a little while.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Funny, I've never thought to open a door like that before.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Come along. Let's take a peek inside.
Guest Room, Veterans' Residence
It's a rather ordinary guest room.
Except there's a peculiar white marble chair sitting by the window. It has a red button on the armrest.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hmm?
The marble feels familiar, but no memories come to mind.
Odd how they both have some kind of familiarity with this place.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Hmm, what's this red button on the chair?
The button seems totally out of place, as if daring someone to press it.
Kimberly takes a seat and curiously presses the button.
*click—click* *click-click-click*
Despite her fervent pressing, nothing happens. Frustrated, she swings her legs over the other side of the chair.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Heh. Good for nothing!
A tasteless decoration. No one knows why this chair is in the doctor's room.
But pressing the button didn't trigger an explosion or anything of the like. It's simply a functionless, harmless little contraption.
On the other side of the room, the doctor's desk holds a stack of manuscripts.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: These must be articles that she hasn't sent out yet.
Notes on the districts of São Paulo, records of arcanists in the favelas, investigations into plantation economies in northeastern Brazil …

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: She's a good woman.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: And her room smells like a good woman's room. You don't find many of those around these days.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What makes you say so?

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Well, firstly, she did save your life.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: And secondly, it's hard to explain. Good people have a smell, a pleasant one. My nose has never been wrong.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Vertin ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We'll bring her home safely.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: This typewriter seems like it's seen a lot of use.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do you see any drafts? Any samples?

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: I can't say. I'm not very familiar with these things.

items.speaker: Ms. Kimberly
items.text: Take a look! She's signed something here. Hmm, but I thought her name was Dores.
There's a single word written at the bottom of the manuscript.
Urd.
Mariana!!
A familiar voice echoes from outside.
TO BE CONTINUED…
